messages:
Emma: Quick question — when a region hits soft quota do we prefer (a) routing to the same-tier model in a different region, (b) falling back to a cheaper model in the same region, or (c) honoring a per-tenant override if present? Trying to pin down the order for the console UX + API behavior.

Raj: my vote is tenant overrides first, then regional spillover to same tier, then cheaper model fallback. otherwise customers who set overrides get surprised. :+1:

Sophie: agree with overrides-first. Can we also distinguish between soft quota (auto-spill) vs hard quota (reject)? UX should show what happened.

Mike: Important: for free tier we probably want cheaper-model fallback before cross-region to save costs. For enterprise, cross-region is better (lower latency/regulatory). So order should be policyable by customer tier.

Emma: yea that matches product thread. So default order by tier: free -> [cheaper-in-region, spill-region], pro -> [spill-region, cheaper-in-region], enterprise -> [spill-region, preserve-model]. But allow tenant-level override that can reorder.

Raj: Implementation note: routing engine currently evaluates global policies then region policies then tenant policies. We'll need to flip that to check tenant policies first. That might be a small change but affects cache keys for prefixes.

Sophie: Also need to decide how quotas are enforced: soft quota should trigger telemetry event and optional spill. Hard quota returns 429 unless a tenant override permits overflow. Telemetry should include which fallback path was chosen for per-request debugging.

Mike: UX idea — in Console -> Routing -> Policy editor show a priority list with drag handles and a preview that simulates "If region X is at 95% capacity, what happens to request Y?" Helps support teams test tenant overrides.

Emma: can we encode a minimal policy JSON for the API so the infra folks can wire it? Example below: 

```json
{
  "name": "tenant_override_example",
  "priority": ["tenant_override","region_spill","cheaper_fallback"],
  "per_tier": {
    "free": ["cheaper_fallback","region_spill"],
    "pro": ["region_spill","cheaper_fallback"],
    "enterprise": ["region_spill","no_fallback"]
  },
  "quota_behavior": {
    "soft": "emit_telemetry_and_spill_if_allowed",
    "hard": "deny_unless_override"
  },
  "spill_policy": {"allow_cross_region": true, "max_latency_ms": 600}
}
```

Raj: that looks good. A couple of questions: how do we represent 'no_fallback' for enterprise? Also need an explicit field for 'respect_data_residency' so we don't violate KMS/region constraints.

Sophie: add a boolean per-tenant: "allow_cross_region_fallback": true/false and a list of allowed model_variants ordered by preference.

Mike: Edge case: if tenant_override allows cross-region but target region is at hard quota too — should we try global fallback model or fail? I'd say try global cheaper model if the tenant allows fallback; otherwise fail.

Emma: agreed. For logging: add fields on the request trace: chosen_path (tenant_override|region_spill|cheaper_fallback|deny), reason, target_region, model_variant, latency_budget_ms. That will make Console traces clearer.

InfraBot: deploy queued: routing-policy-service change (check-tenant-first) -> stage -> canary. PR: https://git.internal/redwood/routing/merge/3456 :bell: 

Raj: I'll post a short changelog entry and update the runtime tests to assert cache key invariants.

Sophie: I'll mock the Console preview with a couple of saved scenarios (free/pro/enterprise) and include an override toggle.

Mike: can we add a metric tag fallback.path so we can graph frequency by tier and path? That will let ops tune defaults.

Emma: yes, metrics + traces + UI preview. Ops: add an alert if cheaper_fallback for enterprise > 1% of requests for 5m.

Raj: timeline: infra PR today, runtime tests + canary tomorrow, console preview next week. Anyone object?

Mike: no objections. +1

Sophie: no objections.

Emma: thanks — I'll file a small product doc and attach the policy schema to the PR.

Raj: noted.

InfraBot: canary deploy succeeded (10% traffic) :white_check_mark:

Emma: awesome, thanks everyone!
